papers.title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
papers.abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.

papers.title: HALO: Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records
papers.abstract: Learning from extensive longitudinal clinical records--spanning repeated encounters, evolving conditions, and heterogeneous documentation--under a finite labeling budget requires solving two coupled problems: deciding what evidence to keep and deciding which patients deserve higher-fidelity labels. Prior work on active learning and multi-fidelity label acquisition mainly addresses the second problem, while treating the evidence presented to the acquisition policy as fixed. We present HALO, a Hierarchical Evidence Selection and Reinforcement Learning pipeline for Allocating Budgeted Label Optimization from Longitudinal Clinical Records. This framework jointly learns what to read and what label source to acquire under budget. HALO first selects informative evidence from longitudinal records and then uses a budget-aware policy to allocate free-, silver-, and gold-fidelity label sources. For frozen policies, our theory characterizes asymmetric acquired-label channels and gives a budget-constrained finite-sample gold-risk bound for a common downstream logistic model. In a heart-failure case study, HALO attained the highest MedAlign acquired-label F1 at six of eight target budgets. A downstream classifier trained on HALO-acquired labels attained the highest external MGB F1 at budgets 15-60 and remained within 0.01 of the best comparator at budgets 75-120.

papers.title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
papers.abstract: We test whether Koopman structure, linear dynamics in a lifted state space, helps when a humanoid whole-body tracking policy is trained by backpropagating through a differentiable world model, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline for simulated Unitree G1 tracking. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train a policy; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the curvature of the true dynamics in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, giving up the structure. The MLP world model thus remains the better choice here.

papers.title: EPIC: Differentiable Energy-Force Consistent Uncertainty Quantification and Propagation for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now rival density functional theory in accuracy and are increasingly used to screen vast crystal databases, yet they can produce unreliable predictions for chemistries outside their training distribution without clear warning. Existing force-level evidential approaches do not inherently define a corresponding uncertainty model over the potential energy surface, limiting the consistent propagation of uncertainty to energy-derived observables. Here we introduce Energy-Propagated Intrinsic Confidence (EPIC), a general energy-centered evidential framework that derives forces as exact gradients of the predicted mean energy, ensuring conservative force fields while providing an analytical estimate of energy uncertainty. Coupled to a MACE backbone trained on the Materials Project trajectory dataset, EPIC propagates uncertainty diagnostics to equations of state, anisotropic structural uncertainty ellipsoids, and phonon dispersions through a Monte Carlo procedure. Applied to 10,966 candidate crystals, the fraction classified as robustly dynamically stable increases from 11\% in the highest-uncertainty quartile to 53\% in the lowest-uncertainty quartile. Furthermore, element-resolved analysis reveals a pronounced chemistry dependence in the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and predicted dynamical stability, highlighting potential limitations in the description of complex bonding environments. EPIC thus provides a physics-aware, chemistry-sensitive uncertainty diagnostic for high-throughput screening and autonomous materials discovery.

papers.title: A Reproducible Reconstruction and Evaluation Framework for Photorealistic Lunar Analog Scene Reconstruction Toward Digital Twins
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a reconstruction pipeline that empirically quantifies the photorealistic scene reconstruction accuracy from both human-controlled and rover mast camera monocular feeds against physical ground truth as a function of Lunar traversal effects (e.g., motion blur, haze due to lofted regolith, trajectory bias, and sparse views). First, we benchmark six variants of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) across three Lunar analog scenes on held-out test sets using standard photometric metrics. We then establish how under traversal effects, this test-set-specific Novel View Synthesis (NVS) performance does not proportionally scale to the same photometric metrics in the reconstructed DTs. Our results quantify that splat training metrics alone are insufficient predictors of Cross-Reconstruction Photorealistic NVS Fidelity (CRPNVS), and that factors such as rover trajectory bias and geometric scene coverage play a critical role in determining the photorealistic quality of the reconstructed scenes targeting Lunar analog Digital Twins. Additionally, we pilot study Coverage Score ($S_c$), a geometry-based diagnostic derived from COLMAP poses and point cloud structure that provides a meaningful heuristic about the highest achievable CRPNVS structural fidelity, independently of splat training performance in the absence of a human-controlled reference. These findings establish a standardized, human control-referenced evaluation pipeline for photorealistic scene reconstruction for Lunar-analog Digital Twin development and future planetary exploration. Code and project page: https://rose-lab-admin.github.io/rose-lunar-dt-rec

papers.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
papers.abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

papers.title: Roz: A Taste Test for World Model Latents
papers.abstract: State of the art latent dynamics world models achieve impressive performance for robot planning. But do they actually encode the physics of the world?   In this paper, we show that popular world models today achieve strong results on tasks that reduce to image similarity but forget key details about objects in the scene like mass, deformation, friction, and bounciness. We achieve this by defining precisely what ought to be encoded in such a world model and introducing two new evaluation methods that can directly tease physical properties and easily scale to new ones. Our evaluation, which we call Roz, includes 10 contrastive tasks and 3 continuous tasks, totaling 1734 individual scenarios. We validate our eval on control tasks. On our own model, AnonWM, we find that performance roughly improves with training steps, while not necessarily being correlated with reconstruction MSE.   We argue current model failures are a symptom of evaluation strategies (probes and planners) that are opaque, model-specific, and high-compute. Roz requires only a model that can ingest still frames or video, a way to extract latents, and a distance function between them, and it can be run in one pass. We hope future evaluations will adopt Roz's evaluation techniques. More broadly, we hope Roz can be a case study for a future where benchmarks allow rapid iteration and comparison across models.

papers.title: Can agents reliably design therapeutic antibodies?
papers.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated agents driving protein design workflows, either through orchestration of specialized tools or direct manipulation of sequences. Yet the fidelity with which agents follow protein design instructions and the factors contributing to their effectiveness remain understudied. We examine agentic antibody design under two settings: when explicit molecular-editing instructions are provided and when agents receive only previously-scored sequences and are prompted to propose improvements. We call the first task-guided and the second black-box design. For the task-guided setting, we curate ten expert-validated affinity-improvement tasks and show that LLM judges closely reproduce programmatic evaluations of instruction following. We then study two augmentations: access to antibody-relevant tools and to previously scored design history. Tools improve instruction following (IF) and sequence space exploration while reducing optimization performance, whereas design history reduces IF but improves optimization performance at the expense of exploration. Finally, we combine taskguided and black-box design within an in silico optimization loop and show that our agentic optimizer performs comparably to an established Bayesian optimization baseline.

papers.title: RIXS study of strain-tuned coupled valence and spin-state transition in epitaxial $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ films
papers.abstract: Strain-tuned $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ thin films provide a model system for controlling coupled valence, spin-state, structural and metal-insulator transitions (VSSTs) in perovskite cobaltite materials. Here, we use Co $L_{2,3}$ and Pr $M_{4,5}$ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), along with Co $L_{3}$ edge Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS), to probe the local electronic structure across the strain-controlled VSST in epitaxial (Pr,Y,Ca)CoO$_{3}$ thin films. In compressively strained films on YAlO$_{3}$ (YAO) substrates, cooling through the transition produces Pr$^{4+}$-like spectral weight, suppresses Co$^{4+}$-like character, and favors predominantly low-spin Co$^{3+}$. The changes at the Pr and Co edges are quantitatively consistent with a reduction of approximately 0.15 holes per Co in the Co--O network. By contrast, tensile-strained thin films on La$_{0.18}$Sr$_{0.82}$Al$_{0.59}$Ta$_{0.41}$O$_{3}$ (LSAT) substrates have nearly temperature-independent spectra. Multiplet calculations reproduce the principal XAS lineshapes and local $dd$ excitations at high energy loss. Additionally, low-energy RIXS intensity recovered above the transition is consistent with a combination of Co$^{4+}$-like local excitations and a broader particle--hole continuum associated with the metallic phase. These results provide element-resolved evidence for charge compensation between the Pr and Co--O sublattices and support cooperative coupling among charge-transfer, spin-state, and lattice structure at the strain-controlled VSST.

papers.title: WorldSketch: Sketching World Models for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Most agentic robotic systems use vision-language models (VLMs) either to orchestrate predefined skills or to directly generate actions, constraints, and control programs. The former is limited by the available skill library, while the latter requires VLMs to reason about precise geometry and contact. In this paper, we propose WorldSketch, a new paradigm for agentic robotics in which a VLM constructs a world model rather than generating robot actions. The VLM acts as an agent that actively queries perception tools to build and visually validate a minimal kinematic world model, capturing only task-relevant objects, their interaction geometry, and possible motions. A geometric planner then jointly optimizes contact and whole-body motion on the resulting model. Moreover, the world model is self-improving: execution feedback verifies outcomes, updates uncertain hypotheses, and enables the agent to revise the model when its predictions are contradicted. We demonstrate the generality of this paradigm across RoboCasa, LIBERO-PRO, and R2R-CE navigation, achieving zero-shot success rates of 91%, 97%, and 76%, respectively. On RoboCasa, WorldSketch outperforms the next-best zero-shot agent baseline by 58 percentage points while using 10 times fewer VLM input tokens; on LIBERO-PRO, it exceeds CaP-X by 82 percentage points. In navigation, it matches the success rate of step-by-step VLM agents while using 6 times fewer input tokens.

papers.title: Hip joint condition before total hip arthroplasty in patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases who had not previously received or had received biological therapy
papers.abstract: Aim : To conduct a comparative analysis of the state of the hip joint before total hip arthroplasty (THA) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis who had not previously received and had received biological drugs. Materials and methods . The retrospective study included 458 patients (170 with ankylosing spondylitis and 288 with rheumatoid arthritis). Among the patients with ankylosing spondylitis, there were predominantly men (80.6%), and in rheumatoid arthritis – women (84.4%). The mean age was 38.1±11.3 and 42.4±9.6 years, respectively. The duration of hip pain before THA in patients with ankylosing spondylitis was 7.4±4.8 years, and in patients with rheumatoid arthritis – 5.6±3.2 years. Preoperative functional state of the hip was assessed using the modified Harris Hip Score, and macroscopic changes in the femoral heads and acetabulum were assessed intraoperatively. The participants were divided into two groups: group 1 – bio-naive patients (n=371) and group 2 – those with experience of biological drugs (n=87). Results. Preoperative assessment of the overall Harris Hip Score revealed worse hip joint function in the bio-naive group. Patients in this group also reported significantly higher hip pain levels, as assessed by the Harris Hip Score and visual analog scale. Objective assessment of hip motion by the physician revealed similar levels of functional limitations in these joints in both groups. Intraoperative assessment of the acetabulum also revealed no significant differences between the groups. Bio-naive patients were less likely to have partial absence of articular cartilage on the femoral head and joint ankylosis, and more likely to have chondromalacia. Conclusion . Patients using biologic drugs have better functional status of the hip joint than biologic-naive patients, which opens up prospects for increasing rehabilitation potential and reducing the recovery period after surgery.

papers.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Explainable Interactive Digital Twin for Student Performance Prediction and Model Governance
papers.abstract: While explainable AI and interactive machine learning can enhance transparency in predictive systems, many existing methods only provide limited support for continuous monitoring, diagnosis, adaptation, and governance of deployed prediction models in higher education. The paper presents a human-in-the-loop explainable interactive digital twin for student performance prediction and predictive model lifecycle management. It consists of four operational modules: model performance monitoring, course-level investigation, interactive model adaptation, and what-if simulation. Based on an already validated eLSTM student grade prediction model, the system provides the capability for educational personnel to monitor model health across courses, check prediction behaviour via SHAP and LIME explanations, review underperforming models, simulate possible interventions, and assess candidate model modifications prior to deployment decisions. Instead of being a static prediction interface, this digital twin helps facilitate transparent human oversight of the behaviour and adaptations of the predictive model under changing educational conditions. A pilot study reveals that the system is found useful, understandable, and supportive in facilitating responsible AI adoption based on academic decisions. This work provides a model for a practical operational framework that has elements of explainability, human-guided model investigation, interactive adaptation, and deployment governance, thereby expanding the scope of student performance prediction from a standalone analytics task toward an adaptive and trustworthy decision-support capability.

papers.title: Effect of Heat Treatment on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Medical-Grade ELI Ti64 Alloy Additively Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.abstract: Medical-grade extra-low-interstitial Ti64 alloy (ELI Ti64) is a promising material for biomedical implants, and additive manufacturing facilitates the fabrication of complex implant geometries. However, additively manufactured ELI Ti64 typically exhibits insufficient ductility, necessitating heat treatment to tailor its microstructure and properties. In this work, we selected three temperatures near the α′-phase decomposition point (800 °C, 850 °C, 900 °C) to investigate how closely spaced heat treatment temperatures affect the microstructure and properties of manufactured ELI Ti64 alloy via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). The manufactured ELI Ti64 alloy consisted mainly of acicular α′ martensite with only 0.3% of the β phase. Annealing promoted the α′ → α + β transformation. At 800 °C, α′ decomposed only partially; at 850 °C, α′ fully decomposed into lamellar α and short rod-like β; at 900 °C, the α laths coarsened and the β-phase content increased to 4.6%. The average α/α′ grain size increased from 1.71 to 2.48 μm, corresponding to approximately 45.03% coarsening. With increasing annealing temperature, strength decreased while elongation increased. The LPBF-manufactured ELI Ti64 alloy exhibited a yield strength of 1004 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 1054 MPa, and an elongation of 10.4%. The product of strength and elongation (PSE) increased from 10.96 GPa·% for the LPBF-manufactured condition to 13.4, 19.7, and 20.9 GPa·% after annealing at 800, 850, and 900 °C, respectively. The 900 °C/2 h + furnace cooling treatment achieved the best strength–ductility combination for tensile behavior, with an 89.60% improvement in PSE compared with the LPBF ELI Ti64 alloy. These results demonstrate that even within a narrow annealing temperature window, the microstructure and mechanical properties of LPBF-manufactured ELI Ti64 can be effectively tailored.

papers.title: A Study on Improving the Educational Effectiveness of a Fire and Extinguishing Theory Course Using Havruta-Based Active Learning
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine changes in the educational effectiveness of learners after applying Havruta-based active learning to a theory course in a fire service major. Question-centered Havruta and peer-teaching Havruta were applied for 60 minutes in each of four class sessions of the course "Fire and Extinguishing Theory," taken by 47 first-year students in the Department of Fire Service Administration. Following a one-group pretest-posttest design, academic self-efficacy and self-directed learning ability were measured before and after the intervention. Data were analyzed using paired samples t-tests, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and Pearson correlation analysis. The results showed that academic self-efficacy increased significantly from 3.13 to 3.68 (t=10.779, p<.001) and self-directed learning ability from 3.09 to 3.67 (t=9.886, p<.001), with significant improvements observed in all six subfactors. Learners' perception of the Havruta classes was positive at 3.87, while their perceived burden of the activity was low at 2.04. However, no significant correlation was found between the individual Havruta performance index and the educational effectiveness indicators, suggesting that participation itself, rather than the level of performance, may be associated with the observed changes. This study contributes by presenting a case and operational procedure for applying Havruta to a theory course in a fire service major, although the absence of a control group limits causal inference.

papers.title: Analisis Karakteristik Sekolah yang Efektif untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar Siswa di SDN 2 Sukarame
papers.abstract: This study aims to analyze the characteristics of effective schools in improving the learning outcomes of elementary school students at SDN 2 Sukarame. The study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data collection techniques include observation, interviews, and documentation, with informants comprising the principal, teachers, students, and parents. Data analysis was conducted using the Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña model through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. The results of the study indicate that the characteristics of an effective school at SDN 2 Sukarame include participatory leadership by the principal, a positive school culture, teacher professionalism, a conducive learning environment, the use of learning media, and parental involvement in student education. The principal’s leadership plays a crucial role in fostering a collaborative work culture, improving the quality of learning, and promoting the development of teachers’ competencies. A school culture characterized by discipline, literacy, and character development has a positive impact on student motivation and discipline. Teachers have implemented active learning and utilized educational media to enhance student understanding, although the implementation of educational technology still faces challenges due to limited facilities and teachers’ digital competencies. Additionally, parental involvement through communication and collaboration with the school also supports improvements in student learning outcomes. This study concludes that school effectiveness is shaped by the integration of leadership, school culture, teacher professionalism, the learning environment, instructional innovation, and sustained parental support. The findings of this study are expected to serve as a reference for improving the quality of basic education and strengthening effective schools in the Society 5.0 era.

papers.title: Penerapan Model Active Learning Tipe Team Quiz Dalam Meningkatkan Keaktifan Belajar Peserta Didik Kelas IV Pada Pembelajaran IPAS
papers.abstract: Keaktifan belajar peserta didik kelas IV pada pembelajaran IPAS materi Gaya di Sekitar Kita belum merata dan baru berkategori Cukup Aktif karena pembelajaran didominasi ceramah dan keterlibatan hanya muncul dari beberapa peserta didik. Penelitian tindakan kelas ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan peningkatan keaktifan belajar, hasil belajar, dan keterampilan mengajar guru setelah penerapan model Active Learning tipe Team Quiz. Penelitian mengikuti desain Kemmis dan McTaggart dengan prasiklus (satu pertemuan) dan dua siklus yang masing-masing terdiri atas tiga pertemuan, pada 17 peserta didik kelas IV SDN 1 Prambatan Lor. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket keaktifan belajar (24 pernyataan), tes evaluasi tertulis, lembar observasi keterampilan mengajar guru, dan catatan pengamatan kualitatif, lalu dianalisis secara deskriptif komparatif. Tindakan dinyatakan berhasil apabila minimal 75% peserta didik berkategori Aktif atau Sangat Aktif, setiap aspek angket minimal 75%, ketuntasan klasikal minimal 75%, dan keterampilan mengajar guru minimal Baik. Rata-rata keaktifan belajar meningkat dari 60,17% (prasiklus) menjadi 64,77% (Siklus I) dan 84,01% (Siklus II); proporsi peserta didik berkategori Aktif atau Sangat Aktif naik dari 41,2% menjadi 70,6% dan 100%. Rata-rata nilai evaluasi naik dari 62,06 menjadi 70,59 dan 88,24 dengan ketuntasan klasikal 100% pada Siklus II, sedangkan keterampilan mengajar guru naik dari kategori Cukup (69,86%) pada Siklus I menjadi Sangat Baik (88,75%) pada Siklus II. Seluruh indikator keberhasilan tercapai pada Siklus II. Penerapan Team Quiz diikuti peningkatan keaktifan belajar peserta didik, tetapi karena tidak ada kelompok pembanding, hubungan sebab-akibat belum dapat dipastikan.

papers.abstract: This conceptual study examines the application of constructivist theory in teaching Arabic to non-Arabic speakers at Pondok Pesantren Jawaahirul Falah, Pati, with a focus on teaching strategies, the role of the teacher, and their educational implications. Constructivism emphasizes that learners actively construct knowledge through experience, interaction, exploration, and reflection rather than simply receiving knowledge from the teacher. In Arabic language learning, this approach places learners at the center of the educational process and encourages them to use Arabic in meaningful and real-life situations. Drawing on the relevant literature, the study proposes a conceptual design of constructivist teaching strategies for this pesantren context, including problem-based learning, inquiry and discovery learning, cooperative learning, the use of sensory and technological media, continuous feedback, contextualized learning, and varied classroom activities. It also explains the changing role of the teacher from a primary source of information to a facilitator, guide, organizer of an active learning environment, provider of learning resources, motivator, and assessor who considers individual differences among learners. The study further provides an illustrative example of a lesson entitled “At the Market,” in which students learn vocabulary and communication skills through dialogue, role playing, shopping list activities, picture word matching, short video recordings, and discussions about everyday prices. Based on this theoretical review, constructivist learning is expected to increase students’ active participation, confidence, communication skills, critical thinking, and ability to connect Arabic with their daily lives. Although its implementation is likely to require more preparation time, more comprehensive assessment, and greater teacher involvement, constructivist learning is argued to provide a more interactive, meaningful, and enjoyable environment for Arabic language learning. Thus, constructivism can support the development of practical Arabic language skills by enabling learners to learn through experience and use the language as part of their everyday lives.

papers.abstract: Strengthening honesty in Islamic Religious Education (IRE) and Character Education is important amid digital conditions that make information readily accessible while also creating risks of academic dishonesty. Studies of deep learning in IRE have discussed meaningful, mindful, and joyful learning, but have provided limited detail on how learning experiences relate to observable dimensions of honesty and how evidence of character development is assessed. This study examines the implementation of deep learning and the process of strengthening honesty among Grade 10 students at SMA Kornita IPB, Bogor. It uses a qualitative case study design. Participants comprised one IRE teacher, one Guidance and Counseling (GC) teacher, and six Grade 10 students. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation, and documentation. Thematic analysis involved repeated reading, initial coding, grouping codes, developing themes, and cross-checking findings through source and method triangulation. The findings identify three stages of learning: participatory planning, active learning through case studies and role-play, and reflection through muhasabah. The study contributes a context-specific account of honesty development across three dimensions: appropriation of rules, academic integrity, and personal responsibility, supported by teacher role modelling, habituation, and school collaboration. Because the study is a single case and character assessment was not systematically documented, the findings do not establish causality or long-term change. Future research should examine structured assessment tools and trace character development longitudinally.

The participants were 30 Grade 9 students from Ban Kanit PeeRuangkhao, Selected randomly from a population normally distributed. The research instruments included (1) lesson plans based on PBL integrated with gamification, (2) an activity suitablility evaluation form and (3) a trigonometry achievement test. The data were analyzed using percentage, mean, standard deviation and a dependent-sample t-test. The findings revealed that 1) the developed learning activities were highly appropriate, characterized by problem-solving scenarios and gamified motivational element, 2) students’ post-test scores were significantly higher than their pre-test scores at the .01 level and 3) students demonstrated greater enthusiasm and engagement in learning. The study indicates that integrating PBL and gamification effectively enhances students’ mathematics learning achievement and fosters intrinsic motivation toward active learning.

The research instruments were questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. The data were analyzed using percentage, mean, standard deviation, PNImodified, and content analysis. The findings revealed that: 1) the overall priority need for promoting learning management in an era of global disruption was at PNImodified = 0.136. papers.title: Artroplastia: fatores associados à falha precoce do implante
papers.abstract: Objective: To analyze the main factors associated with early implant failure in arthroplasty, considering clinical implications and strategies to prevent complications and improve prosthetic survival. Methods: An integrative literature review was conducted using the PubMed, SciELO, Revista Brasileira de Ortopedia, NIH, Medscape, and Google Scholar databases. Studies published between 2019 and 2026 in Portuguese and English were included, using the keywords "arthroplasty," "implant failure," "early implant failure," "complications," and "risk factors." After applying eligibility and exclusion criteria, 35 articles comprised the final sample. Results: Early failure was characterized primarily by loss of fixation, instability, or aseptic loosening within the first year post-surgery. Associated factors included periprosthetic infection, inadequate bone quality, incorrect implant positioning, early mechanical overload, and low primary stability. Male gender, higher functional demand, and the presence of pathogens that are difficult to eradicate were also associated with failure. Conclusion: Early implant failure in arthroplasty has a multifactorial etiology involving biological, mechanical, technical, and clinical aspects. Rigorous surgical planning, appropriate implant selection, and early identification of risk factors are essential to reduce complications, avoid revision surgeries, and improve clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Tailoring Wicking and Fluid Transport Properties in Laser Powder Bed Fusion Additively Manufactured Aluminum Alloy Lattice Structures for Heat Transfer Systems
papers.abstract: Additively manufactured lattices allow the capillary and hydraulic properties of a wick to be set by design, but the combined effect of lattice architecture and chemical post-processing on fluid transport in aluminum alloys is not well established. Twelve AlSi10Mg lattices were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) in body-centered cubic (BCC) and face-centered cubic (FCC) architectures with unit cell sizes of 1.5 and 2.0 mm and strut diameters of 0.30–0.40 mm. Porosity, steady-flow pressure-drop permeability, and capillary rise in methanol were measured before and after a 90 s sodium hydroxide etch; measured pressure gradients were compared with numerical simulations. As-built porosity was 3–12% below the design value because of adhered powder; etching restored it to within about 5%. Permeability normalized by the square of the strut diameter increased exponentially with porosity, and BCC lattices were two to four times more permeable than FCC lattices of the same dimensions. Etching increased the permeability of the FCC lattices by a factor of 1.5–2.1 but reduced the capillary rise height in most specimens by up to 38%. Simulated pressure gradients were within 20% of the measurements for BCC lattices but under-predicted those of FCC lattices by 11–51%. Overall, properly controlled chemical etching reduced the discrepancy between simulated and measured pressure gradients. These findings identify a trade-off between hydraulic permeability and capillary rise within the tested configurations and treatment conditions; device-level thermal performance remains to be evaluated.

papers.title: Digital inclinometer-guided acetabular cup positioning in total hip arthroplasty: A prospective observational study
papers.abstract: Proper acetabular cup alignment during total hip arthroplasty (THA) is essential to reduce instability, impingement, wear and loosening, but advanced navigation systems are often unavailable because of their cost and limited accessibility. This prospective study evaluated 30 patients undergoing THA between May 2024 and April 2026 using a dual-axis digital inclinometer for intraoperative cup inclination and post-operative radiographic inclination and Harris Hip Score at 6 months were assessed. Post-operative radiographs showed that 27 of 30 hips (90%) were within the Lewinnek safe zone and the mean post-operative inclination angle was significantly lower in the safe group than in the unsafe group (42.34 +/- 3.00° vs. 55.91 +/- 4.26°, p < 0.05). Patients with cup placement within the safe zone had better Harris Hip Scores (86.22 +/- 8.64 vs. 81.00 +/- 6.08), while a weak positive correlation was observed between intraoperative and post-operative inclination measurements (r = 0.360, p = 0.060). Thus, digital inclinometer-assisted cup placement is a simple, practical and cost-effective technique that may improve acetabular cup alignment during THA, particularly in centres without navigation facilities.

papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) delivers significant advantages for manufacturing medium-/high-entropy alloys (MEAs/HEAs), owing to its near-net-shape manufacturing and the ability to fabricate complex geometries. In this paper, a series of (CoCrNi)100−xTix (x = 0, 1, 2, 4 wt.%) MEAs were successfully fabricated by L-PBF technology, and the effect of Ti addition on the microstructure and mechanical properties was systematically investigated. The results show that L-PBF CoCrNi-4wt.%Ti alloy processed with a laser power of 275 W and the scanning speed of 1000 mm/s delivered a high yield strength of 777.5 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 1054.5 MPa, along with a ductility of 20.8%. Compared with the L-PBF CoCrNi alloy, the CoCrNi-4 wt.%Ti alloy shows an increase in yield strength from 684.8 to 777.5 MPa and in ultimate tensile strength from 961.1 to 1054.5 MPa, accompanied by a decrease in uniform elongation from 27.8% to 20.8% (a reduction of seven percentage points, approximately 25% relative). The present work offers a promising pathway to improve the performance of additively manufactured medium-entropy alloys.

papers.title: Role of platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) in enhancing implant stability in immediate implants
papers.abstract: Immediate implant placement has gained popularity due to reduced treatment time and increased demand for rapid aesthetic outcomes, yet challenges such as reduced primary stability, early bone loss and delayed osseointegration remain. Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), an autologous concentrate rich in growth factors, has shown potential in enhancing both hard and soft tissue healing. This randomised controlled clinical trial involving 50 patients evaluated the effectiveness of PRF in improving implant stability, marginal bone levels, soft tissue healing, peri-implant complications and patient-reported outcomes. Immediate implants were placed in two groups-PRF and non-PRF-and assessed using resonance frequency analysis (ISQ) over 12 weeks, with radiographic bone measurements taken at 3 and 6 months. The PRF group showed significantly higher ISQ values, reduced marginal bone loss, superior soft tissue healing and lower post-operative pain scores compared to controls (p < 0.05). Thus, we show that incorporating PRF into immediate implant placement enhances stability, accelerates healing, improves patient comfort and reduces peri-implant bone loss, offering a simple, cost-effective adjunct for improving clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Parameterization-dependent uncertainty quantification in adjoint-based history matching of channelized reservoirs
papers.abstract: History matching channelized reservoirs is severely ill-posed: a single best-fitting model is of limited value without an estimate of its uncertainty. We present a verified Python framework for adjoint-based history matching of multiple-point-statistics (MPS) channelized fields, and quantify how the parameterization shapes the inferred posterior. The two-phase simulator and its hand-derived, analytically transposed discrete adjoint are verified against a reference simulator, against closed-form and manufactured solutions, and to second-order Taylor-remainder accuracy (slopes ), without automatic differentiation of the simulator. Under an identical adjoint, optimizer and observation set we compare a truncated principal-component analysis (PCA) basis and a variational autoencoder (VAE) on three independent MPS truths, with a cell-wise Direct arm run as a control that carries no spatial structure. Reinterpreting adjoint multistart minimization as randomized maximum likelihood (RML), we show that the parameterization controls the geometry of the entire posterior, not only the point estimate. Across -member ensembles on the primary truth the unstructured Direct arm fits the data as well as PCA yet recovers only well-centered speckle (median correlation ). An excellent data fit does not determine the field. The reduced arms recover structure, with comparable posterior means ( PCA, VAE). The VAE returns the sharpest fields but the narrowest, overconfident posterior, whereas PCA under its Karhunen–Loève prior returns smoother fields and the better calibrated posterior (P10–P90 coverage versus , nominal ), an ordering preserved on every truth. A representation floor, measured by decoding the encoded true field, explains why the VAE cannot always reach the noise floor. The main comparison matches the arms in latent space alone; running all three from one shared set of geological realizations removes that asymmetry and leaves the ordering unchanged. The VAE recovers the field better than PCA on of (paired ). The results frame the parameterization as the effective prior over the data-null space.

papers.title: Strain partitioning and coordinated deformation in dual-region NiTi alloys fabricated by laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Spatial control of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) parameters provides a route to regional property variation in NiTi alloys, but the associated strain partitioning remains insufficiently understood. Three uniform conditions and three dual-region combinations were fabricated by varying the scanning speed, and regional deformation was examined by digital image correlation during room-temperature monotonic tension. Ni loss and transformation temperatures decreased with increasing scanning speed, whereas the pseudo-yield stress varied nonmonotonically, with maximum differences of 64 MPa among the uniform specimens and 54 MPa among the dual-region specimens. Early interregional strain differences reached approximately four percentage points. Two strain-partitioning histories were observed: continued strain separation, and initial separation followed by partial convergence and renewed separation. A two-member trilinear serial model, calibrated using uniform-specimen responses and regional strain differences, reproduced the principal trends, although discrepancies remained in turning-point positions and later strain accumulation. Within this model, three characteristic-stress orderings permit thirteen slope-sign sequences, grouped into six evolution modes of interregional strain difference. The pseudo-yield stresses determine the onset of preferential deformation, while active plateau and hardening compliances govern subsequent strain increments. Characteristic strain-difference endpoints distinguish partial convergence from synchronization or an exchange of the strain-leading region. These relations provide preliminary criteria for selecting regional tensile responses and deformation sequences in stepwise NiTi architectures under quasi-static monotonic loading.

papers.title: Short-Term Solution Treatment of LPBF Fe–Cr–Mn–Mo–N High-Nitrogen Duplex Stainless Steel: Microstructure and Tensile Response of Two Initial States
papers.abstract: Insufficient ductility and processing-dependent mechanical properties limit laser powder bed-fused (LPBF) high-nitrogen stainless steels. This study investigated short-term solution treatment of an Fe–Cr–Mn–Mo–N duplex stainless steel using two as-built samples with distinct microstructures and elongations. Samples were treated at 1050 and 1100 °C for 10 min and water quenched. Microstructure and deformation behavior were characterized by electron backscatter diffraction, tensile testing, loading–unloading–reloading experiments, and transmission electron microscopy. Treatment increased the austenite fraction from 16.0 and 21.1% to 70.8–77.0%, producing an austenite-dominated duplex microstructure with residual ferrite as short strips or isolated islands. Differences in tensile properties between the initial states decreased substantially, with ultimate tensile strengths of 1030.9–1049.9 MPa and elongations of 29.45–33.82%. A representative sample treated at 1100 °C achieved 1030.9 MPa and 33.82% elongation. Its back stress showed an overall increase during plastic deformation, indicating a contribution of long-range internal stresses to strain hardening. Early deformation involved planar slip and localized stacking faults in austenite. Further deformation produced denser planar defects and local 9R structures in austenite, with pronounced dislocation tangles in ferrite. Short-term solution treatment thus enhanced ductility while retaining approximately 1 GPa strength and reducing property discrepancies between initial LPBF-built states.

papers.title: Interplay Between Oxygen-Dependent Marangoni Convection and Recoil Pressure in Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Ti-15Zr Alloys
papers.abstract: Ti-15Zr alloys offer favorable biocompatibility, and interstitial oxygen provides an attractive pathway for further strengthening. However, the interaction between oxygen-modified Marangoni convection and evaporation-induced recoil pressure during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) remains insufficiently understood. A three-dimensional multiphysics thermal-fluid model incorporating recoil pressure and temperature- and oxygen-dependent surface tension was developed. Surface-tension-only, recoil-pressure-only, and coupled simulations were compared on an idealized solid substrate, followed by discrete powder-bed simulations. Increasing oxygen content shifts the dominant Marangoni flow from outward spreading to inward convergence. Recoil pressure primarily drives central depression, whereas Marangoni convection redistributes molten metal. In transverse sections, low-oxygen outward flow competes with recoil-driven downward transport and promotes lateral spreading, whereas high-oxygen inward flow reinforces downward circulation. In longitudinal sections, reversed Marangoni flow suppresses recoil-driven rearward transport and promotes recirculation behind the vapor depression. papers.title: Stealthy Sensor Attacks on IoT-Enabled Model Predictive Control of Perishable-Goods Production: Residual-Based Detection, Mitigation, and Secure Sensing Design
papers.abstract: IoT-enabled model predictive control (MPC) lowers cost and spoilage in perishable-goods production but depends on sensor data that an attacker can falsify, which network intrusion detection cannot verify. We study sensor attacks on a published IoT-MPC plant model and a defense that needs no additional model: a CUSUM test on the innovations of the Kalman filter already in the loop, isolation of flagged sensors, and re-estimation from the attack onset. With accurate sensors and an exact model, a falsified energy meter raises the tracking cost by 71% and replay raises spoilage by 27%; the defense detects them in 89% and 100% of runs at a nominal 1% false-alarm rate and limits the cost increases to 9% and 3%. In closed loop, static detectors miss moderate and slow attacks that predictive detectors find. Detection weakens with sensor noise and model error; a fully informed attacker raises the cost by 93% undetected, but model errors expose it, and a redundant meter on an independent path limits it to about 15%. On the HAI testbed, an identified-model residual detector finds 32 of 34 attacks at 0.24 false alarms per day, against 27 for a windowed autoencoder and 21 for a static range check.

papers.title: Metal Additive Manufacturing for Automotive Applications: Technologies, Materials, Industrial Uses, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (MAM) offers automotive manufacturers design and supply-chain options, but published demonstrations do not by themselves establish production readiness or economic advantage. This critical narrative review connects process selection, alloy behaviour, component requirements and the complete manufacturing chain. It covers laser powder bed fusion, directed energy deposition, binder jetting and metal material extrusion, distinguishing direct vehicle parts from tooling, repair and spare parts. The synthesis identifies the following three recurring constraints: fatigue performance cannot be inferred from tensile strength; sintering-based routes require control of shrinkage and local defects; and printing productivity must be separated from output of accepted finished parts. Published examples include a 10% piston mass reduction and a 17% moulding-cycle reduction, both reported by industrial sources rather than established as sector-wide effects. A requirement-led selection framework, condition-specific material benchmarks and a qualitative economic assessment connect these findings to engineering decisions. The strongest opportunities occur where functional integration, avoided tooling or asset-life extension offset qualification and post-processing costs. Evidence remains heterogeneous and the initial single-database search limits coverage; the review therefore does not claim a systematic census or a universal ranking of technologies. Adoption should be judged at the level of a qualified alloy–process–part combination against a credible conventional alternative.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Mathematical Models Using Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: The discovery of governing mathematical equations directly from observational data represents a pivotal challenge in modern computational science. Traditional model derivation relies on prior physical knowledge and manual hypothesis testing, processes that are increasingly impractical for complex, high-dimensional systems. This paper presents an AI-Driven Mathematical Discovery (AI-DM) framework that integrates deep learning, sparse regression, Gaussian process inference, and symbolic regression to autonomously identify governing differential equations from noisy, limited observational data. The proposed framework employs a four-stage pipeline: feature engineering with physics-informed normalization, latent-space representation learning via variational autoencoders, sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy), and symbolic refinement through genetic programming. Evaluated on five canonical partial differential equations the Lorenz system, heat equation, Burgers' equation, Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation, and Navier-Stokes equations AI-DM achieves a mean R² of 0.944 and RMSE of 0.039, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and classical SINDy. Discovered equations exhibit coefficient-level accuracy within 0.87% relative error. The framework operates without prior knowledge of equation structure and remains robust under 15% additive Gaussian noise, demonstrating broad applicability to scientific model discovery in biology, fluid dynamics, and material science.

papers.title: Multi-Timescale Coordinated Power Allocation and Temperature Control for Wind-Powered Multi-Stack PEM Electrolysis Systems
papers.abstract: Power allocation in wind-powered multi-stack proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolysis depends on both load-dependent efficiency and thermal response. This study evaluates coordinated allocation, stack rotation and temperature control for four parallel 200 kW stacks. A control-oriented model couples electrochemical and thermal dynamics with rectifier losses and hydrogen compression power. Particle swarm optimisation determines the allocation, an equivalent health index guides stack rotation, and model predictive control (MPC) tracks temperature references from an offline stack-efficiency map. Predicted polarisation voltages differ from experimental data by no more than 1.4% at 313 and 333 K. In annual simulations, rotation reduces the cross-stack index standard deviation from 725.10 to 2.92 h. MPC achieves a simulated temperature-tracking root mean square error of 0.019 K, 91.12% below that of fuzzy proportional–integral–derivative control. Across three representative wind power scenarios, the probability-weighted daily hydrogen production is 199.85 kg, 0.59% above optimal allocation at 333 K. The corresponding increases over equal and sequential allocation are 1.26% and 2.43%, respectively. These results quantify the additional hydrogen yield from load-dependent temperature control and the operating-load balance obtained through stack rotation under the evaluated conditions.

papers.title: Effect of osteoporosis on implant stability and peri-implant bone changes
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis may adversely affect peri-implant bone remodeling and osseointegration, potentially compromising implant stability and long-term treatment outcomes. This prospective comparative study evaluated 100 patients, including 50 healthy and 50 osteoporotic patients, by assessing implant stability using resonance frequency analysis and peri-implant marginal bone loss radiographically over 6 months. Osteoporotic patients showed significantly lower implant stability quotient values and greater marginal bone loss than healthy controls (p<0.05), while implant survival remained high and comparable between groups. Osteoporosis negatively affected implant stability and peri-implant bone remodeling without significantly compromising implant survival during follow-up. These findings advance knowledge by supporting careful patient selection, appropriate treatment planning and close follow-up to achieve predictable implant outcomes in patients with osteoporosis.

papers.title: Titanium degradation and peri-implant tissue health: A review
papers.abstract: Titanium and its alloys are widely used in dental implants because of their strength, corrosion resistance and predictable osseointegration. However, corrosion, mechanical wear and tribocorrosion can release titanium particles and ions into peri-implant tissues, potentially contributing to inflammation and marginal bone loss. Therefore, it is of interest to examine the titanium degradation mechanisms, particle distribution and biological pathways involving macrophage activation, cytokine release, osteolysis and inflammasome signalling. Diagnostic challenges include the absence of validated biomarkers and limited evidence establishing a direct causal relationship between titanium degradation and peri-implantitis. Thus, improved diagnostic methods, surface modifications, antimicrobial coatings and alternative implant materials may help reduce degradation-associated tissue damage and improve long-term peri-implant health.

papers.title: Explainable offline process analytics for within-grade quality variability in industrial rubber mixing
papers.abstract: In industrial rubber mixing, the nominal quality grade of a product is largely governed by the production recipe and is well understood by experienced operators.However, batches manufactured within the same grade may still exhibit significant quality fluctuations, whose origins are difficult to identify due to the combined influence of recipe settings, material characteristics, process variables, equipment conditions, and environmental factors.This work addresses an upstream offline analysis problem: identifying and interpreting variables associated with within-grade quality variability in high-dimensional industrial data.The proposed framework uses predictive modeling as an analytical backbone for robust feature selection, explainability analysis, interaction discovery, and uncertainty-aware interpretation.It combines Ranked Frequency Feature Selection (RFFS), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based global, local, and pairwise interaction explainability, and Conformal Prediction (CP)-based Uncertainty Quantification (UQ).The framework is validated on a large-scale Michelin rubber-mixing dataset comprising 35,125 production records and 316 input variables, including Production Recipe Settings (PRS), Process Variables (PV), Weather Conditions (WC), and Raw Material Characteristics (RMC).The proposed feature-selection strategy identifies a compact subset of 53 variables, corresponding to an 83% reduction of the original input space, while reducing Mean Squared Error (MSE) by 17%; the selected variables reveal that PRS and RMC, rather than traditional PV, are the primary drivers of quality variability.SHAP analyses reveal influential variables, threshold effects, and interactions among key descriptors, while CP provides statistically calibrated prediction intervals with guaranteed marginal coverage.Complementary to an in-process soft sensor, the framework provides an offline, explainable, and uncertainty-aware methodology for extracting process knowledge from accumulated industrial production records, supporting variable prioritization, process investigation, and quality improvement.

papers.title: Peran Guru Dalam Penerapan Pendekatan Pembelajaran Deep Learning Pada Mata Pelajaran IPAS Terhadap Kemampuan Komunikasi Siswa Kelas V SD
papers.abstract: Communication skills are among the 21st-century skills that need to be cultivated during Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) instruction in elementary schools. However, some students remain passive when it comes to expressing opinions, asking questions, or participating in discussions during the learning process. While previous research has largely focused on the impact of deep learning on academic outcomes, studies regarding the teacher's role in implementing deep learning to foster students' communication skills in elementary IPAS lessons remain limited. This study aims to describe the teacher's role in implementing the deep learning approach and its effect on the communication skills of fifth-grade elementary students. This study employed a descriptive qualitative method using a case study approach. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, involving one fifth-grade teacher and five students as subjects. Data analysis utilized the Miles and Huberman model, with validity verified through source and technique triangulation. The findings indicate that the teacher acts as a facilitator, guide, motivator, and mediator in fostering active learning through discussions, question-and-answer sessions, group work, and presentations. The application of mindful, meaningful, and joyful learning principles supports student engagement in developing communication skills. This study serves as a reference for elementary school teachers in designing deep learning-based IPAS instruction that is more interactive, meaningful, and student-centered.

papers.title: Cyber-physical security and resilience in microgrids: a comprehensive review of attack scenarios, detection methods, and defense mechanisms
papers.abstract: The rapid transition toward renewable-dominated energy systems has transformed microgrids (MGs) into highly interconnected cyber-physical systems (CPSs), where advanced communication, intelligent control, and inverter-based resources enhance operational flexibility while introducing unprecedented security vulnerabilities. This paper presents a comprehensive review of cyber-physical security and resilience enhancement strategies for MGs by establishing a unified framework that integrates attack scenarios, detection methodologies, and defense mechanisms. The evolving threat landscape is systematically analyzed, including false data injection, denial-of-service, spoofing, replay, and coordinated hybrid attacks targeting communication infrastructures, control layers, and physical power dynamics. Furthermore, existing detection approaches are critically reviewed and categorized into model-based, statistical, artificial intelligence and machine learning-based, physics-informed, and digital twin-enabled frameworks. Particular attention is given to emerging techniques such as deep learning, reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, federated learning, and physics-informed neural networks, highlighting their potential and limitations under nonlinear and uncertain inverter-dominated operating conditions. Defense and resilience strategies are investigated through secure communication, adaptive control, redundancy, attack mitigation, self-healing operation, and recovery-oriented approaches. The review further emphasizes the importance of real-time validation platforms and digital twins for predictive risk assessment and autonomous cyber-physical resilience management. Finally, key research challenges are identified, including scalability, explainability of intelligent security models, realistic hardware-in-the-loop validation, standardized resilience metrics, and the development of integrated physics–AI frameworks for future secure and adaptive MGs.

papers.title: Physics-model-derived ANN–GA surrogate optimization of membrane electrode assembly thickness in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers using a reduced-order electrochemical model
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) have emerged as a highly promising technology for sustainable green hydrogen production because of their high energy efficiency, rapid dynamic response, and compatibility with intermittent renewable-energy systems. However, the optimization of membrane electrode assembly (MEA) structural parameters remains challenging because of the highly coupled nonlinear electrochemical and transport phenomena governing PEMWE performance. In the present study, a physics-model-derived surrogate framework integrating a one-dimensional (1D) reduced-order electrochemical model with an artificial neural network–genetic algorithm (ANN–GA) optimization strategy was developed to investigate and optimize PEMWE electrochemical behavior. The proposed reduced-order model incorporated reversible thermodynamics, activation polarization, proton transport resistance, and porous-media mass-transfer limitations while maintaining substantially lower computational cost than multidimensional multiphysics simulations. The model was experimentally validated over operating temperatures ranging from 40 to 80 °C and current densities between 150 and 750 mA·cm −2 . Excellent agreement between model predictions and experimental measurements was achieved, with voltage-prediction RMSE values of 0.092–0.156 V, MAPE values below 5 %, and R 2 values exceeding 0.93. For hydrogen production prediction, RMSE values ranged from 7.8775 to 9.6920 mL·min −1 with R 2 values greater than 0.96. Sensitivity analysis revealed that membrane thickness exerted the strongest influence on PEMWE voltage behavior because of its direct impact on proton transport resistance and ohmic losses. Subsequently, 5000 datasets generated from the validated electrochemical model were employed to train a multilayer feedforward ANN surrogate model. The optimized ANN architecture achieved exceptional predictive capability with near-unity regression coefficients (R ≈ 0.99997) and extremely low prediction errors across the training, validation, and testing datasets. The trained ANN was then integrated with a genetic algorithm to perform rapid multi-parameter optimization of PEMWE operating and structural conditions. The optimal configuration corresponded to a current density of 775.7223 mA·cm −2 , membrane thickness of 25.0572 µm, anode porous transport layer thickness of 150.2763 µm, cathode porous transport layer thickness of 339.2383 µm, anode catalyst-layer thickness of 24.9891 µm, and cathode catalyst-layer thickness of 24.9980 µm, yielding ANN-predicted outputs of 2.3198 V and 146.2061 mL·min −1 for cell voltage and hydrogen production rate, respectively. Independent verification using the reduced-order electrochemical model demonstrated discrepancies below 2 % within the sampled model domain. The optimum is a numerical design candidate rather than an experimentally demonstrated configuration because its membrane thickness and current density extend beyond the experimental calibration range and gas-crossover and durability constraints were not included. The developed methodology provides a computationally efficient, scalable, and physically interpretable tool for accelerated PEMWE design optimization and next-generation green hydrogen system development.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Design of High Entropy Oxides for Photo-Electrocatalysis and Sustainable Energy Conversion
papers.abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) offer a vast compositional platform for photo-electrocatalysis and sustainable energy conversion, where multicationic disorder can tune phase stability, electronic structure, defect chemistry, light absorption, charge transport, and surface reactivity. However, the enormous number of possible compositions, local configurations, and synthesis conditions limits conventional trial-and-error discovery. This review critically evaluates how machine learning (ML) accelerates HEO design, from phase and structure classification, oxygen-vacancy prediction, machine learning interatomic potentials, and active learning to photocatalytic, electrocatalytic, thermocatalytic, and energy-storage applications. Unlike earlier surveys, it grades the evidence by separating studies that report accurate ML predictions from those in which ML-selected HEOs were synthesized and shown to perform; benchmarks representative models together with their dataset sizes and validation procedures; and draws on high-entropy alloy catalysis to show how local atomic environments shape adsorption-energy distributions, reaction barriers, and selectivity. This appraisal shows that functional validation of ML-selected HEO catalysts has so far been achieved mainly for CH4 oxidation, the water–gas shift reaction, and the oxygen evolution reaction, whereas photocatalytic H2 evolution and CO2 conversion still lack prospective ML validation. Key challenges include biased datasets, incomplete synthesis metadata, inadequate representations of local disorder, and uncertain applicability domains. Finally, complementary validation categories and a minimum reporting standard are proposed to support reliable ML-guided discovery of synthesizable HEOs for sustainable energy technologies.

papers.title: Robust Trajectory Tracking of a Flying-Wing UAV: A Comparative Evaluation of Optimized Smooth Sliding Mode, PID, and MPC Controllers
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comparative framework for robust trajectory tracking of a Skywalker X8 flying-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) using optimized smooth sliding mode control (SSMC), cascaded proportional–integral–derivative (PID) control, and model predictive control (MPC). The controllers are evaluated on a nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom UAV model incorporating a high-fidelity aerodynamic representation derived from wind-tunnel measurements and flight-test-informed refinements. The SSMC employs a cascaded outer–inner-loop architecture with smooth nonlinear switching functions, while PID and SSMC parameters are optimized using derivative-free pattern search, and the constrained linear MPC benchmark is tuned using Bayesian optimization. Performance is assessed under nominal, stochastic-wind, and sensor-noise conditions at multiple climb rates, with additional Monte Carlo and empirical disturbance-scaling analyses. MPC provides the highest tracking precision and the lowest actuator effort under nominal and wind-disturbed conditions, but its tracking error and control effort increase most strongly under sensor noise. SSMC consistently improves upon optimized PID, particularly in tracking quality, transient behavior, and saturation, and yields the lowest tracking error and control effort under sensor noise. Empirical disturbance-scaling tests further show that PID and SSMC tolerate substantially larger wind amplification than MPC within the simulated horizon. Overall, SSMC provides a favorable compromise between tracking performance, actuator demand, and disturbance robustness.

papers.title: Machine Learning Forecasts of Groundwater Recharge Stress in a Semi-Arid Kovilpatti Region, Southern India
papers.abstract: Groundwater recharge in hard-rock semi-arid terrains depends more on how rainfall is distributed through the year than on its total amount, yet most drought and recharge indices rely primarily on rainfall totals. This study addresses that gap for Kovilpatti region, Tamil Nadu, a crystalline-aquifer, rain-shadow region utilising 125 years (1901-2025) of India Meteorological Department gridded daily rainfall data. A dynamic Recharge-Stress Index (dRRSI) was built from four indicators, SPI-12 deficit, maximum dry-spell length, precipitation concentration index and rainy-day deficit, combined through entropy weighting, which assigned 84% of total weight to rainfallstructure variables. Trend and change-point analysis identified a significant increasing rainfall trend and an abrupt regime shift in 1987 (+25.5% mean annual rainfall), corroborated by an independent rainfall typology. Eight forecasting models were benchmarked at 1, 3, 6 and 12-month lead times. The skill was strong at short horizons (Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency above 0.75 up to three months) but collapsed below the climatological baseline by 12 months. SHAP attribution showed forecasts shift from short-term memory toward rainfall-structure variables as horizon lengthens. Three uncertainty quantification methods all under-covered their nominal 90% target. These findings suggest that recharge stress in such systems is genuinely forecastable only over the short-to-medium term.

papers.title: Implementing Online Synchronous Learning in Private Elementary Schools: Impact on Students’ Independent Learning and Challenges in Tagbilaran City Division
papers.abstract: This study examined the implementation of online synchronous learning in three private elementary schools of Tagbilaran City Division during school year 2021–2022, focusing on its impact on students’ independent learning and the challenges encountered by teachers and parents. A descriptive qualitative research design was employed to understand how schools, teachers, and parents maximized limited resources to support learners during the new normal. Data were purposively gathered from ten private elementary school teachers and ten parents through an open-ended Google Forms survey and semi-structured virtual interviews, then examined using Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase manual thematic analysis. Findings showed that schools relied on key instructional resources, such as learning activity sheets, worksheets, performance tasks, textbooks, and summative tests, and supplemental learning resources, comprising digital tools and devices. Online synchronous learning was found to positively influence students’ independent learning through a cognitive-behavioral impact—serving as a catalyst for self-regulated learning, academic integrity, and active learning support—and through an affective impact that fostered a sense of community and motivation. However, implementation was hindered by technological difficulties, particularly poor internet connectivity; physical and digital distractions; and personal and psychological barriers, such as low motivation and poor comprehension and retention. The study concludes that online synchronous learning is a valuable strategy for cultivating independent learning, but its success rests on sustained collaboration among teachers, parents, and learners. It recommends engaging learning materials, active learning strategies, stronger home-school communication, and a capability-building and monitoring program to help sustain the modality.

papers.title: Dental implant hemocompatibility: Comparison of two surface treatments
papers.abstract: Implant surface topography can influence the initial blood-surface interaction that precedes osseointegration. Therefore, it is of interest to compare the hemocompatibility of 14 commercially available titanium implants with calcium-phosphate-blasted surfaces (Group I, n=7) or alumina-blasted and acid-etched surfaces (Group II, n=7) using blood-cell counts, platelet measures and platelet adhesion/activation assays. Initial-to-final paired comparisons were not statistically significant in either group (Group I p=0.551; Group II p=0.488), while platelet adhesion/activation was numerically higher for the calcium-phosphate-blasted surface (409.94 +/- 884.62 vs 352.79 +/- 723.63 IU/L). The reported hemolysis values are unusually high for conventional hemocompatibility interpretation and should be verified against the original laboratory calculation and units before submission. Thus, surface-dependent variation in early blood interactions, but the present results do not establish statistically significant superiority of one surface treatment.

papers.title: Evaluating success rate of implants in patients with controlled Diabetes mellitus: A prospective comparative clinical study
papers.abstract: Dental implant therapy in patients with diabetes remains clinically challenging because hyperglycemia can alter bone healing, osseointegration and peri-implant inflammatory responses even when systemic disease is considered controlled. This prospective comparative study evaluated 120 adults receiving a single posterior implant, including 60 participants with controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c 6.5-8.0%) and 60 metabolically healthy controls, with standardized placement and 12-month follow-up. At 12 months, implant survival was 98.3% in the controlled-diabetes group and 100% in controls, while strict implant success was 95.0% and 98.3%, respectively; the between-group differences were not statistically significant (p>0.05). Controlled-diabetes participants showed a modestly greater mean marginal bone loss (0.71 +/- 0.29 mm vs 0.56 +/- 0.24 mm, p=0.003) and slightly higher bleeding on probing, but implant stability remained high and no clinically important difference was detected in probing depth or suppuration. Thus, carefully selected patients with controlled type 2 diabetes achieved high implant survival and success, although closer peri-implant maintenance is justified because early crestal bone and inflammatory changes may be greater than in non-diabetic individuals.

papers.title: AI-based prediction of implant prosthesis micromotion under simulated mastication: An in vitro study
papers.abstract: Cyclic loading can alter implant-abutment settling, screw preload and prosthesis micromotion, while instability is governed by interacting mechanical variables. Therefore, it is of interest to develop and test a machine-learning model for predicting prosthesis instability after simulated masticatory cycling in 120 implant-supported zirconia crowns with internal conical, internal hex, or external hex connections. Digital image correlation, reverse-torque assessment, marginal-gap measurements and 200,000 loading cycles at 100 N were used and gradient boosting incorporated connection design, insertion torque, preload loss, marginal gap, baseline micromotion and cycle-stage features. Thirty assemblies met the instability definition; the test-set model achieved an AUC of 0.93, sensitivity of 86.7%, specificity of 88.9% and Brier score of 0.10, with baseline micromotion, post-settling torque loss and connection type as the strongest predictors. Thus, machine learning identified fatigue-related instability in this controlled model, but independent external validation is required before mechanical decision support is considered.

papers.title: Precision tissue engineering in implant rehabilitation - A randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Implant positioning influences osseointegration, peri-implant tissue health and esthetic outcomes. Therefore, it is of interest to compare the digitally guided and conventional freehand placement in 100 implants, with 50 implants per group. Guided placement achieved lower angular, coronal and apical deviations than freehand placement (p<0.001). At 12 months, guided placement showed higher implant stability, lower marginal bone loss, improved peri-implant parameters, greater keratinized mucosa and higher Pink Esthetic Scores (p≤0.027). Thus, guided implants also showed higher survival (98% vs. 92%), supporting precision-guided placement for predictable peri-implant tissue and esthetic outcomes.

papers.abstract: Osseointegration depends on early bone-implant interactions, which may be influenced by surface wettability. This prospective study compared 62 hydrophilic and hydrophobic implants in 48 healthy adults using resonance frequency analysis at placement and 2, 4 and 8 weeks. Hydrophilic implants showed significantly higher stability at 2 and 4 weeks, with comparable values by week 8. At 8 weeks, marginal bone loss was lower with hydrophilic surfaces (0.41 +/- 0.19 mm versus 0.58 +/- 0.24 mm; p = 0.004), with 100% implant survival. Thus, hydrophilic surfaces may enhance early implant stability and reduce marginal bone loss, although longer follow-up is needed.
