papers.title: Order vs disorder in 3D-printed bone scaffolds: A critical review on the gap between engineered regularity and native extracellular matrix complexity
papers.abstract: Large bone defect repair remains a persistent clinical challenge. Although three-dimensional (3D) printing has enabled unprecedented control over scaffold architecture, the anticipated breakthrough in functional bone regeneration has not yet been fully realized. This critical review interrogates a foundational but largely untested assumption in scaffold design: that increasing geometric control inherently enhances biological fidelity. Recurrent limitations, including stress shielding, inadequate vascularization, and confined cellular infiltration, persist across ordered architectures ranging from cubic lattices to optimized triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMS) and Voronoi-based structures. These failures appear to stem from a single conceptual gap: the distinction between optimization for geometric predictability, an engineering objective, and optimization for functional heterogeneity, an evolutionary solution. To address this gap, the native extracellular matrix (ECM) is reframed not as a passive physical scaffold but as an active multidimensional information system in which disorder reflects purposeful organization rather than noise. The concept of "intelligent disorder" is introduced to describe the hierarchical, anisotropic, and locally heterogeneous nature of bone ECM, features often overlooked in conventional biomimetic design. The central question is therefore not which ordered architecture is optimal, but whether complete geometric order is an appropriate paradigm for mimicking a tissue that has evolved through controlled heterogeneity. A paradigm shift is proposed: from designing for order and predictability to designing for controlled functional complexity, offering a new conceptual foundation for next-generation bone scaffolds.

This study employed a descriptive approach using a needs analysis method, involving 142 Package B learners in Musi Banyuasin Regency selected through purposive sampling, with data collected using a seven-point Likert-scale questionnaire consisting of 60 statements. The results indicated a high need for e-module development, with an average score of 5.2 out of 7 and an ideal percentage of 73.6%; the three highest-scoring aspects were technology and applications (77.3%), self-efficacy (77.2%), and active learning based on the Internet of Things (74.4%), alongside the identified connection between blacksmithing practices and the concepts of temperature and heat. Therefore, developing an e-module based on blacksmith ethnopedagogy is necessary as a contextual and interactive digital teaching resource that addresses the needs of Package B learners. papers.title: Enhancing Grade 8 Students’ Thai Reading Comprehension through SQ4R-Based Active Learning and Reading Skill Exercises
papers.abstract: This study examined changes in Thai reading comprehension among Grade 8 students following SQ4R-based active learning with reading exercises. The objectives were to evaluate instructional efficiency against a 75/75 criterion, compare pretest and posttest scores, calculate an effectiveness index, and assess student satisfaction. A one-group pretest–posttest design involved 40 students from one intact classroom selected through cluster random sampling at a public secondary school in northeastern Thailand. The intervention comprised six lesson plans delivered over 12 hours and followed six stages: Survey, Question, Read, Record, Recite, and Reflect. Reading exercises addressed main-idea identification and comprehension of informational, persuasive, and literary texts. Data were collected using formative assessment records, a 30-item multiple-choice reading comprehension test, and a 15-item satisfaction questionnaire. Analyses included descriptive statistics, process and outcome efficiency percentages, an effectiveness index, and a paired-samples t test. Process and outcome efficiency values were 86.17% and 78.33%, respectively, exceeding the specified criterion. Mean reading comprehension scores increased from 13.63 (SD = 5.16) to 23.50 (SD = 2.40), t(39) = 11.53, p < .001. The mean increase was 9.88 points, with a 95% confidence interval of [8.14, 11.61]. The effectiveness index was .6031, representing 60.31% of the maximum possible gain from the pretest baseline. Overall satisfaction averaged 4.71 out of 5. The findings provide preliminary evidence of improved reading performance and favorable learner perceptions following the intervention. However, the absence of a comparison group and the reuse of test items limit causal interpretation.

papers.title: Safe reinforcement learning force control for a hydraulic actuator with real-world training using a learned contraction metric
papers.abstract: Force control in hydraulic actuators remains challenging because of strong nonlinearities, uncertainties, and the risks associated with unsafe exploration during learning. This work examines safe reinforcement learning (RL) for hydraulic force control with real-world training using contraction-metric certificates. A data-driven model of the hydraulic actuator, identified from experimental data, is used for simulation-based pre-training of Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policies that adapt the gains of feedback-linearization (FL) and sliding-mode control (SMC) force controllers. To limit instability during online training, we propose a quadratic-programming (QP) contraction filter that uses a learned contraction metric to enforce an approximate contraction condition in the force-tracking direction while introducing minimal corrections to the policy output. The framework is validated on a hydraulic test bench, where RL policies are trained directly on hardware and benchmarked against fixed-gain and simulation-trained counterparts. The experimental results indicate that real-hardware training mitigates the gain over-optimization and instability observed in simulation-only policies, with the most evident benefits appearing for the SMC-based learning controller. The results further show that the proposed method does not consistently outperform well-tuned fixed-gain controllers in all operating conditions, especially when the nominal model is already accurate. These findings suggest that contraction-based certificates can support safe RL in high-force hydraulic systems, while also emphasizing the local and task-dependent nature of the learned safety certificate.

papers.title: LLMVisExplorer: Visually exploring the knowledge landscape of large language models
papers.abstract: The performance of large language models (LLMs) in specific knowledge domains is often evaluated based on question and answer (Q&A) benchmark datasets. Although benchmark reports sometimes include domain-level breakdowns, evaluation results are still frequently summarized through aggregate accuracy values or coarse tables that make it difficult to inspect multi-level, multi-metric, and question-level performance variation. This is problematic because Q&A benchmark datasets are by design diverse and span broad domains, such as science (SciQ) or biomedicine (PubMedQA). We argue that overly coarse evaluation summaries can collapse meaningful details: strong performance in easier or overrepresented areas can overshadow weaknesses in critical or complex subdomains, making such summaries insufficient for downstream use. To enable better understanding of real-world model capabilities essential for downstream applications, we propose LLMVisExplorer, an interactive visualization system that facilitates in-depth evaluation of LLM performance within the subdomains of complex knowledge domains. Based on LLM evaluation design requirements grounded in the natural language processing (NLP) literature, LLMVisExplorer bridges the gap between coarse-grained benchmark reporting and actionable model insights by enabling multifaceted, visually guided performance analysis across hierarchical knowledge domains. It empowers both, LLM developers and LLM users, to identify domain-specific strengths and weaknesses, in order to inform model development, red-teaming, and deployment decisions. We discuss LLMVisExplorer’s design requirements as well as its realization, and showcase its potential on several use cases evaluating single models as well as comparing multiple models, such as Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Yi-large. LLMVisExplorer’s source code and data will be provided upon acceptance.

papers.title: Regular meets random: A smooth connection between TPMS and Voronoi lattice in 3D printed bioceramic scaffolds
papers.abstract: Micro-architected materials are nowadays ubiquitous in many engineering applications, where high performance and simultaneous optimization of multiple functional properties are required. In the field of bone tissue engineering, scaffolds are used to restore bone continuity within defect sites. These defects often span regions with different characteristics, ranging from cortical to trabecular bone. Consequently, an effective scaffold must incorporate spatially distinct architectural regions to mimic the heterogeneous environment of the host tissue. Combining Voronoi-based and TPMS-based architectures offers a promising strategy to recreate two fundamentally different micro-architected environments. However, a smooth and continuous transition between a regular periodic structure (TPMS) and a stochastic structure (Voronoi) has not been reported in the literature yet. In this study, a topology optimization algorithm has been employed to generate a smooth connection between the two architectures within a design composed of two concentric cylindrical regions. Finite element models were developed to identify potential stress concentrations within the hybrid scaffold: three loading conditions (i.e., uniaxial compression, radial compression, and torsion) showed that the transitional region does not exhibit high stress concentrations, confirming its structural soundness. Finally, to demonstrate the manufacturability of the proposed architecture, the scaffolds were fabricated using vat photopolymerization with hydroxyapatite and a hydroxyapatite/calcium phosphate blend. While not intended for a specific anatomical site, this design serves as a challenging test case to evaluate the printing fidelity of architectures characterized by substantially different geometrical features. In both cases, excellent printing fidelity was achieved by a proper printing parameter tuning process, as confirmed through computed micro-tomography analyses.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文将TPMS与Voronoi晶格平滑连接用于3D打印生物陶瓷支架，涉及多孔结构设计与FEA应力分析，与AM生物医学材料方向相关，但未涉及金属植入体或应力遮挡。
llm.why_not_core: It uses vat photopolymerization of bioceramics rather than LPBF metal implants, and reports no stress shielding, fatigue testing, or osseointegration assessment.

summary_zh.motivation: 骨缺损跨越皮质骨与松质骨，需空间异质支架模拟宿主组织。
summary_zh.method: 用拓扑优化生成TPMS与Voronoi双同心圆柱区的平滑过渡，并建FEA模型分析三种载荷下的应力集中。
summary_zh.result: 过渡区无明显应力集中，结构可靠；羟基磷灰石及复合生物陶瓷打印保真度良好。
summary_zh.validation: 有限元应力分析与micro-CT打印保真度表征。

summary_en.motivation: Bone defects spanning cortical and trabecular regions require scaffolds with spatially distinct architectures that mimic the heterogeneous host tissue.
summary_en.method: A topology optimization algorithm was used to create a smooth transition between TPMS and Voronoi architectures in a two-region concentric cylinder, with finite element models under compression, radial compression, and torsion.
summary_en.result: The transitional region showed no significant stress concentrations, and hydroxyapatite-based scaffolds were printed with high fidelity.
summary_en.validation: Finite element stress analysis and micro-computed tomography assessment of printing fidelity.

papers.title: استراتيجية مبتكرة لتعلم اللغة العربية للأجيال الرقمية: دمج التكنولوجيا، الثقافة الرقمية، والمنهجيات التربوية الحديثة
papers.abstract: The development of digital technology in the 21st century has brought significant changes to the characteristics of learners, particularly the digital generation that has grown up alongside information and communication technologies. This condition demands innovation in language learning strategies, including Arabic language instruction, to make the learning process more relevant, interactive, and effective. This study aims to describe innovative Arabic language learning strategies through the integration of technology, the strengthening of digital literacy, and the implementation of modern pedagogical approaches in learning activities at the Special Program for Arabic Language Development (PKPBA) of UIN Maulana Malik Ibrahim Malang. This research employed a qualitative approach using a descriptive method. Data were collected through observations of learning activities, interviews with instructors, and analysis of learning documents used in the PKPBA program. Data analysis was conducted through the processes of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing to obtain a comprehensive understanding of the learning strategies implemented. The findings indicate that Arabic language learning in PKPBA has integrated various digital technologies, including online learning platforms, audiovisual media, and interactive applications that support language skills development. Furthermore, the learning process promotes students’ digital literacy through the utilization of internet-based learning resources, digital project-based assignments, and collaborative activities that make use of communication technologies. From a pedagogical perspective, the strategies employed emphasize communicative approaches, activity-based learning (active learning), and contextual approaches that encourage students’ active engagement in language practice. The integration of technology, digital literacy, and modern pedagogical approaches in Arabic language learning at PKPBA has proven effective in enhancing learning motivation, student participation, and the effectiveness of Arabic language skills acquisition. Therefore, the learning model implemented in PKPBA can serve as a reference for developing Arabic language learning strategies that are adaptive to the characteristics of the digital generation in the 21st-century educational era.

papers.title: Oxidation mechanism of 316L stainless steel manufactured by laser powder bed fusion in highly oxygenated simulated pressurized water reactor coolant
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) is an advanced additive manufacturing technique for producing stainless steel components having intricate geometries. Understanding the oxidation and electrochemical behaviour of L-PBF stainless steels is essential for their potential application in high temperature aqueous environments. This study investigates the influence of stress relieving (SR), solution annealing (SA), and hot isostatic pressing (HIP) on the corrosion behaviour of L-PBF 316 L in an oxygenated simulated pressurized water reactor (PWR) environment. In-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was combined with ex-situ Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and analytical electron microscopy to characterize the electrochemical response and oxide films. Results indicate that post-heat treatment substantially modifies the L-PBF-derived microstructure, including grain-boundary character, cellular dislocation structure, and precipitate morphology, thereby influencing local oxidation pathways and oxide-film characteristics. Cross-sectional observations revealed differences in oxide morphology and thickness among the heat-treatment conditions, whereas the overall electrochemical response remained relatively similar. Mixed-Conductive Model analysis further showed that the differences in the electrochemically detectable transport and interfacial reaction parameters were relatively modest. Under the highly oxidizing test condition, chromium depletion from the inner oxide was promoted, consistent with preferential chromium dissolution and/or redistribution and the development of a Cr-depleted Ni-Fe spinel-rich oxide. Although heat treatment modifies local oxidation behaviour and oxide-film characteristics, these effects do not translate into proportionally large changes in the integrated electrochemical response. The findings provide mechanistic insight into the relationship between heat-treatment-induced microstructural evolution and oxide development of L-PBF 316 L under the investigated highly oxygenated high temperature aqueous conditions.

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to clarify how post-processing heat treatments affect the corrosion performance of additively manufactured stainless steel in high-temperature oxygenated aqueous environments.
summary_en.method: L-PBF 316L specimens subjected to stress relieving, solution annealing, and hot isostatic pressing were characterized using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy combined with Raman spectroscopy, XPS, and analytical electron microscopy.
